A_target.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]] and $A, B \subseteq S$.
Then the [[Definition:Interior (Topology)|interior]] $A^\circ$ is the largest open subset of $A$, with:
:$A^\circ = S \setminus \paren {S \setminus A}^-$
:$\paren {A \cap B}^\circ = A^\circ \cap B^\circ$

B_source.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space and $A, B \subseteq S$.
Then the [[Definition:Closure (Topology)|closure]] $A^-$ is the smallest closed superset of $A$, and:
:$\paren {A \cup B}^- = A^- \cup B^-$

derived.complementation: the dictionary between closure and interior

object_map.reformulation: Complementation reverses inclusion and exchanges open with closed sets, so every closure statement dualizes to an interior statement.

validity_conditions: Complementation is an inclusion-reversing involution of the power set.
De Morgan's laws exchange unions and intersections.
proof_plan: $U \subseteq A$ is open {{iff}} $S \setminus U \supseteq S \setminus A$ is closed.

Hence the largest open subset of $A$ is the complement of the smallest closed superset of $S \setminus A$:
:$A^\circ = S \setminus \paren {S \setminus A}^-$

By [[De Morgan's Laws (Set Theory)|De Morgan's laws]] and the source result:
:$\paren {A \cap B}^\circ = S \setminus \paren {\paren {S \setminus A} \cup \paren {S \setminus B} }^- = S \setminus \paren {\paren {S \setminus A}^- \cup \paren {S \setminus B}^-} = A^\circ \cap B^\circ$

In the same way the [[Definition:Kuratowski Closure Axioms|Kuratowski closure axioms]] dualize to the interior axioms.
{{qed}}
